intro: You are looking for a trusts adviser near you, someone who can help with the specific tax and legal duties that come with running a trust. Whether you are setting up a trust, dealing with its tax returns, or need to register it, a local adviser can guide you through the rules. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK professional who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a trusts adviser near me usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a trusts adviser near them are dealing with the practicalities of setting up or running a trust and want local, expert help.
needs: You are a trustee who has recently taken on the role and need to understand your legal duties and tax responsibilities.
You want to set up a trust for family members and need advice on the type of trust and its tax implications.
You are responsible for a trust that must be registered with the Trust Registration Service and need help with the process.
You need to file a trust tax return or deal with the ten-year charge and want a professional to handle it.
You are unsure whether a trust is the right option for your circumstances and want advice on the tax rules before deciding.
context: Trusts have their own tax rules, and most must be registered with HMRC's Trust Registration Service. Trustees have legal duties, including keeping records and filing returns. A trusts adviser can help you meet these obligations and avoid common pitfalls.

In the UK, 'tax adviser' is not a protected title, so it is wise to check qualifications. The Chartered Institute of Taxation (CTA) and the Association of Taxation Technicians (ATT) are the main specialist bodies, and their members follow Professional Conduct in Relation to Taxation. Tax advisers who charge a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, and HMRC has been tightening standards for paid tax agents. It is reasonable to ask about qualifications, supervision and professional indemnity insurance before you proceed.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when enquiring
tell: Describe the type of trust you are dealing with, such as whether it is a new trust you want to set up or an existing trust you need help with.
Explain what you need help with, for example registration, tax returns, the ten-year charge, or general advice on trustees' duties.
Mention whether the trust is already registered with the Trust Registration Service or if that is something you need assistance with.
State your role, such as trustee, beneficiary, or someone considering setting up a trust.
Include your location so we can introduce you to a professional near you.
Let us know if you have any particular deadlines or time-sensitive issues, without using specific dates if possible.
questions: What qualifications and experience do you have in dealing with trusts and their tax affairs?
Are you a member of a professional body such as the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians?
How do you charge for your services, and what will the likely costs be for my situation?
Will you handle the registration of the trust with the Trust Registration Service if needed?
Can you explain the ten-year charge and how it might apply to my trust?
What information and records will you need from me to get started?

faqs.q: Do I need a trusts adviser if I am a trustee?
faqs.a: Trustees have legal duties and must ensure the trust complies with tax rules, including registration and filing returns. A trusts adviser can help you understand and meet these obligations, especially if the trust has complex tax affairs.

faqs.q: What is the Trust Registration Service?
faqs.a: The Trust Registration Service is HMRC's online system for registering trusts. Most trusts must be registered, and a trusts adviser can guide you through the process and ensure you meet the requirements.

faqs.q: How can I check if a trusts adviser is qualified?
faqs.a: You can ask about their qualifications and membership of professional bodies such as the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians. Also ask about their supervision for anti-money-laundering purposes and professional indemnity insurance.

faqs.q: What is the ten-year charge on trusts?
faqs.a: The ten-year charge is a tax that may apply to certain trusts on each tenth anniversary of the trust's creation. A trusts adviser can explain whether it applies to your trust and help you calculate and pay any tax due.

extra_heading: Finding a trusts adviser near you: what to consider
extra: When you search for a trusts adviser near me, you are likely looking for someone you can sit down with locally, or at least speak to easily, about the trust you are involved with. Proximity can matter if you need to discuss sensitive family arrangements or share paperwork in person, but it is not the only factor. The right adviser for your trust will have relevant experience with the type of trust you have and the issues you are facing.

Trusts come in many forms, from simple bare trusts to complex discretionary trusts, and the tax rules and administrative duties differ accordingly. A local adviser may be convenient, but you should also check that they regularly deal with trusts like yours. Ask how they keep up to date with changes to trust taxation and the Trust Registration Service, and whether they can handle the ten-year charge if it applies.

Before your first appointment, gather the trust deed and any previous tax returns or correspondence with HMRC. This will help the adviser understand your position quickly. At the meeting, you can expect to discuss the trust's tax status, registration requirements, and your duties as a trustee. Be clear about what you want to achieve, whether that is compliance, planning, or simply peace of mind.

extra_faqs.q: Do I need to meet a trusts adviser in person?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many advisers work remotely or offer a mix of phone, video and in-person meetings. What matters most is that you can communicate easily and that the adviser understands your trust's needs. If you prefer face-to-face contact, look for someone local, but don't rule out a specialist elsewhere if they have the right expertise.

extra_faqs.q: How can I compare trusts advisers near me?
extra_faqs.a: Start by checking their qualifications and experience with trusts. Ask about their membership of professional bodies such as the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians, and whether they are supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes. Also ask for a clear explanation of how they charge and what services they will provide, so you can compare like with like.
